newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end firm, bolsa driven by earnings.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end firm, bolsa driven by earnings.

text.p: Chile blue chips closed broadly higher in heavy trade as investors reacted to company first quarter earnings which proved a mixed bag, said traders.
"Today has been one of correction after all the pre-results speculation," said one dealer.
The 40-share .IPSA index ended up 0.38 percent at 118.79 points. The general .IGPA index gained 0.01 percent at 5,331.05 points.
Turnover remained high for the second day running with volume Wednesday of 17.9 billion pesos.
The bolsa will be closed Thursday for the May Day holiday and will reopen at 0930 local time/1430 GMT Friday.
The heavy volume is seen continuing Friday with analysts expecting a wave of profit-taking as investors digest earnings figures.
A number of firms reported poor earnings including telecom Telex, whose net profit plunged to 133 million pesos from 2.05 billion in the same period last year.
Telex inched up 0.47 percent at 1,080 pesos.
Better-than-expected earnings were posted by brewery CCU , which rallied 0.56 percent to 1,800 pesos.
Forestry firm Masisa climbed on news that it has signed a long-awaited deal to buy a 51 percent stake in competing board maker Tableros Nobel, said traders.
Masisa ended up 2.27 percent at 225 pesos. ((-- Margaret Orgill, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595 x212))
